explanation_audit.scope: manual evidence/rationale audit over frozen blind prediction records

architecture_A.comment: Positive/negative statements were authored from frozen candidate facts and training patterns, but A did not preserve exact evidence pointers.

architecture_C.comment: The graph is connected through seven common fixed anchors per candidate, but per-edge explanations were not persisted; candidate-candidate cycles/non-transitivity cannot be tested in this star design.

architecture_D.comment: D preserved record-level provenance labels, not exact fact/profile pointers. Content was manually cross-checked as supported, but traceability is below production evidence-contract quality.

ui_audit.readability: score + interval + one positive + one negative is compact and understandable
ui_audit.critical_issue: readable explanations can still accompany badly wrong scores; Mass Effect was displayed at 100 while hidden truth was 25, so explanation readability must not be confused with score reliability

cost_audit.measurement_note: This ChatGPT/connector run did not expose per-candidate LLM latency or token telemetry. Runtime seconds are therefore not fabricated; semantic decision counts are used as the reproducible cost proxy.

A.description: one holistic calibrated score plus dominant positive and negative rationale

C.deterministic_work: Bradley-Terry grid fit plus Thurstone sensitivity fit

D.description: two evidence findings plus seven pairwise judgments

cost_audit.implementation_observation: All four can be batched into one semantic record per candidate; C/D add deterministic mapping but their semantic comparison burden is materially higher than A.
